standard_prerequisites.name: Every formula has a formation sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Subset direction (proof lines 1299-1300): by prop:formed, Frm(L) is contained in the set of strings having a formation sequence; the theorem proves the converse.

standard_prerequisites.name: Initial segments of formation sequences
standard_prerequisites.use: Inductive case (lines 1321-1323): initial segments (A_0,...,A_j) and (A_0,...,A_k) of the formation sequence are formation sequences for A_j and A_k.

core_obligations: Setup (proof lines 1297-1300): let F be the set of all strings in the language L that have a formation sequence; the containment Frm(L) subseteq F holds by prop:formed, and the converse is proved.

Strong induction (lines 1302-1305): suppose A has a formation sequence (A_0,...,A_n); prove A in Frm(L) by strong induction on n, with the hypothesis that every string with a formation sequence of length m < n is in Frm(L).
Case split (lines 1306-1317): by the definition of a formation sequence, A = A_n is atomic or A equals one of the seven constructions from earlier members A_j (and A_k) with j,k < n.
Atomic case (lines 1318-1319): if A is atomic then A_n is in Frm(L_0) by definition.

Inductive case (lines 1320-1328): for example if A = (A_j land A_k), then by lem:fseq-init the initial segments (A_0,...,A_j) and (A_0,...,A_k) are formation sequences for A_j and A_k, of length less than n; by the induction hypothesis A_j and A_k are in Frm(L_0), hence so is (A_j land A_k); the other cases follow by parallel reasoning.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the converse to strong induction on the length of a formation sequence.
Split by the last member of the sequence: atomic or one of seven constructions.
Handle the atomic case directly and the inductive cases with lem:fseq-init plus the induction hypothesis.
difficulty_reason: Characterization theorem (statement 1290-1294, proof 1296-1330): Frm(L) is exactly the set of L-strings with a formation sequence - the proof runs strong induction on the sequence length, splits on the seven construction rules and the atomic case, and uses lem:fseq-init to shorten the sequence; each inductive case is argued and the remaining cases close by parallel reasoning. H2: routine strong induction with a standard case split.
